Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Which person or organization did Ben F. Spencer work for?
Document 1: "The Academic Trailblazer: Unveiling the Illustrious Career of Ben F. Spencer"

In the esteemed halls of the University of Manchester, a renowned public research university in Manchester, England, a brilliant mind once thrived, leaving an indelible mark on the academic community. Ben F. Spencer, a distinguished researcher, spent a significant portion of his illustrious career within the university's walls, contributing to groundbreaking discoveries and shaping the minds of future generations. As we delve into the archives of the University of Manchester, a treasure trove of evidence emerges, testifying to Spencer's affiliation with the institution. A 1995 issue of the university's staff newsletter, "Manchester Matters," features a article highlighting Spencer's appointment as a Research Fellow in the Department of Physics and Astronomy. This coveted position not only recognized his exceptional expertise but also entrusted him with the responsibility of mentoring students and collaborating with esteemed colleagues. Further investigation reveals that Spencer's research focus on advanced materials and nanotechnology led to several publications in prestigious scientific journals, including the "Journal of Materials Science" and "Nanotechnology." A closer examination of these publications reveals the University of Manchester's affiliation listed alongside Spencer's name, solidifying his connection to the institution. One of Spencer's most notable contributions during his tenure at the University of Manchester was his involvement in the development of a novel nanomaterial with potential applications in renewable energy. This pioneering work, funded by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), was showcased in a 2002 university press release, which quoted Spencer as the lead researcher. The release not only acknowledged his innovative approach but also highlighted the university's commitment to fostering cutting-edge research. In addition to his research endeavors, Spencer's dedication to teaching and mentorship is evident in the numerous student testimonials and evaluations from his time at the University of Manchester. One such evaluation, dated 2005, praises Spencer's ability to "break down complex concepts into accessible, engaging lectures," demonstrating his passion for education and his impact on the academic community. As we weave together the threads of evidence, a rich tapestry of Ben F. Spencer's career at the University of Manchester emerges. From his appointment as a Research Fellow to his groundbreaking research and dedication to teaching, the narrative of Spencer's time at the university is one of academic excellence, innovation, and a lasting legacy.
Document 2: As Dr. Sophia Patel poured over the dusty archives in the basement of Edinburgh Napier University's Sighthill campus, she stumbled upon a forgotten folder with a faded label: "Spencer, B.F. - Research Collaborations (2005-2008)". The name sparked a faint memory, and Sophia's curiosity was piqued. She delicately opened the folder, releasing a whisper of aged paper and forgotten dreams. Inside, she found a collection of yellowed documents, meeting minutes, and scribbled notes. The handwriting was messy, but the ideas were revolutionary. Sophia's eyes widened as she read about Ben F. Spencer's groundbreaking research on sustainable energy harvesting. The concepts were ahead of their time, and Sophia couldn't help but wonder why they had been shelved. As she delved deeper into the folder, Sophia discovered a series of emails between Ben and his colleagues, discussing the potential applications of his research. The tone was enthusiastic, with a hint of frustration. It seemed that Ben's innovative ideas had been met with skepticism by the university administration. Sophia's brow furrowed as she read about the bureaucratic red tape that had slowed Ben's progress. Suddenly, a faint noise echoed from the corner of the archive room. Sophia looked up to see a bespectacled archivist, Mrs. MacTavish, peering over the rim of her reading glasses. "Ah, you've found the Spencer files," she said, her voice laced with a hint of nostalgia. "Ben was a brilliant mind, but a bit of a rebel. He didn't suffer fools gladly." Sophia's eyes locked onto Mrs. MacTavish. "Did you know him?" she asked, her voice barely above a whisper. Mrs. MacTavish nodded, her eyes clouding over. "Aye, I did. Ben was a researcher here at Edinburgh Napier University. He was part of our team, working on a project to develop sustainable energy solutions for rural communities. He was passionate, driven... and a bit of a thorn in the side of our administrators." As Sophia listened, Mrs. MacTavish's words painted a vivid picture of Ben F. Spencer - a maverick researcher who had pushed the boundaries of innovation, even if it meant ruffling a few feathers. The forgotten folder, once a relic of a bygone era, now held a new significance.
